catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted architectural and structural patterns from cas_runner codebase, excluding LLM prompting and agentic workflows.

system_map.overview: cas_runner is a continuous architecture platform consisting of a CLI presentation entrypoint, orchestration engine (FlowRunner), typed domain modeling (governance & steering entities via Pydantic), pluggable service engines (compliance, transition registry), and an external integration boundary (LLM clients and Git delta analysis).

layers.name: Presentation / CLI Layer
layers.purpose: Command-line interface commands handling invocation, parameter parsing, and runtime environment bootstrapping.

layers.name: Application & Orchestration Layer
layers.purpose: Execution flow coordination, lifecycle transitions, and health reporting.

layers.name: Domain Layer
layers.purpose: Strictly typed data definitions, governance models, steering indices, and health status indicators.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Integration Layer
layers.purpose: Adapters for LLM APIs (LiteLLM, Mock), telemetry (OpenTelemetry), and template-based storage operations.

components.name: FlowRunner
responsibilities: Coordinates end-to-end execution passes across the workspace

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine
responsibilities: Evaluates actions and resolves state transitions via TransitionRegistry

components.name: ComplianceEngine
responsibilities: Validates workspace governance compliance against schemas and rules

components.name: SteeringIndex & Capability Models
responsibilities: Encapsulates structural capability lineage, architectural deltas, and git changes

orchestration.details: Linear runner coordinates lifecycle actions, backed by transition registries and rule engines.

state_and_memory.name: File-based Knowledge Repository
state_and_memory.persistence: Markdown templates, YAML runtime profiles, and JSON rule contexts

patterns.name: Pydantic Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Encapsulates architectural governance, steering indices, and health attributes as typed, validated Pydantic models.
patterns.intent: Provide strongly typed schema guarantees and serialization across the file ingestion and runtime boundaries.
patterns.context: The system processes YAML/JSON configuration files, rule contexts, and Git deltas across heterogeneous CLI commands.
forces: Need for schema validation at system boundaries without boilerplate parsing code.
Need immutability or deterministic state inspection across pipeline stages.
patterns.solution: Define domain models (e.g. GovernanceInventory, ComplianceFinding, CapabilityRecord) inheriting from BaseModel with explicit enum typings.
implementation_signals: Use of typing enums such as GitChangeType, CapabilityRecordType, HealthStatus
Direct deserialization of runtime configs into domain models

evidence.note: Defines core architectural governance entities with type validation
Defines steering graph and git change delta structures

benefits: Runtime guarantees on input data integrity.
Automatic serializability to JSON and YAML for trace outputs.
costs: Runtime serialization overhead on large datasets.
Tight coupling of domain definitions to the Pydantic library.
failure_modes: ValidationError exceptions crash CLI operations unless caught explicitly at presentation boundaries.

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be reused across all python-based governance and steering tools.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine
patterns.summary: Decouples lifecycle state mutations and valid governance steps through a centralized transition registry.
patterns.intent: Maintain an extensible registry of allowed architectural transitions and operations without hardcoding conditional branching.
patterns.context: Architectural artifacts progress through varying lifecycle states (e.g., proposed, accepted, deprecated, promoted).
forces: Need to validate that governance actions follow allowable transition rules.
Desire to add new transitions without modifying the core execution engine.
patterns.solution: Implement a TransitionRegistry that holds registered transition rules and provides lookup services to the GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: Separation of TransitionRegistry and GovernanceActionEngine classes
Action registration methods mapping triggers/events to next states

evidence.note: TransitionRegistry maintains allowed transitions consumed by GovernanceActionEngine
Service layer facade invoking action engine transitions

benefits: High extensibility for new workflow rules and state transformations.
costs: Requires indirect invocation via registry rather than direct procedural calls.
failure_modes: Unregistered states or missing transitions lead to unhandled resolution exceptions.

patterns.reuse_notes: Easily ported to any rule-driven workflow engine.

patterns.name: Service Facade Application Boundary
patterns.summary: Provides high-level application service facades encapsulating domain engines for presentation layer consumers.
patterns.intent: Isolate the CLI commands and flow runners from lower-level action engines, registries, and metric collectors.
patterns.context: CLI handlers need to trigger complex governance actions without orchestrating internal engine dependencies.
forces: CLI code should remain thin and focused on CLI parameter parsing.
Internal domain logic should not leak into CLI interface scripts.
patterns.solution: Introduce service wrappers such as GovernanceActionService that encapsulate engine initialization, dependency coordination, and persistence.
implementation_signals: Service classes mediating between presentation/CLI and domain engines
Methods coordinating multiple engines (e.g., engine execution followed by metric recording)

evidence.note: Encapsulates GovernanceActionEngine and provides entry points for CLI runners
Delegates commands to application services and FlowRunner

benefits: Clean separation of CLI presentation logic and core business workflows.
Simplifies unit and integration testing of services without invoking CLI parser.
costs: Additional boilerplate layer when operations are simple passthroughs.
failure_modes: Facade becoming a 'God Object' if all orchestration logic accumulates in single service classes.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard application pattern for modular Python applications.

patterns.name: Polymorphic Client Adapter
patterns.summary: Abstracts external infrastructure integration behind interchangeable client implementations including a test double mock.
patterns.intent: Decouple domain and orchestration services from external network-bound dependencies.
patterns.context: The system relies on external LLM services but needs offline, deterministic execution for testing and local dry runs.
forces: External dependencies are costly, rate-limited, or unavailable during CI/test runs.
Engine code should not change depending on whether running in live or mock mode.
patterns.solution: Expose matching client interfaces with a production adapter (LiteLLMClient) and a test double (MockLLMClient).
implementation_signals: Parallel classes sharing common method signatures (LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient)
Configuration-driven injection of client instance into application runners

evidence.note: Mock implementation providing synthetic responses for deterministic testing

benefits: Enables offline, deterministic execution and end-to-end testing.
Isolates external vendor API shifts to a single module.
costs: Risk of behavior drift between MockLLMClient and real API responses.
failure_modes: Mock client fails to simulate network errors or token limits present in production adapter.

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard architectural adapter pattern applicable across any external service integration.

patterns.name: Pure Functional Metric Evaluation
patterns.summary: Evaluates architectural and dashboard health through stateless calculation functions returning discrete status enums and reasons.
patterns.intent: Maintain pure, side-effect-free calculations for system health status derivation.
patterns.context: Dashboard reporting requires evaluating current system state against health thresholds without modifying system data.
forces: Health checks must be idempotent and easily testable.
Health state evaluation should not depend on file I/O or network connections.
patterns.solution: Implement health calculation as pure module-level functions that accept raw data and return enum statuses with reason lists.
implementation_signals: Functions like calculate_health and get_health_reasons defined with no external side-effects
Return types based on discrete enum classes (HealthStatus)

evidence.note: Pure functions calculating health metrics without mutating state

benefits: Trivial to test with unit tests using parameterized inputs.
Guarantees absence of side effects when generating dashboards.
costs: Caller is responsible for aggregating and passing all necessary state.
failure_modes: Inconsistent threshold parameters if passed from different caller locations.

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt whenever computing status or scoreboards across static analysis artifacts.

patterns.name: File-Backed Template Convention Repository
patterns.summary: Organizes domain governance, rules, and architecture artifacts using hierarchical filesystem conventions and markdown templates.
patterns.intent: Persist evolving architectural decisions, rules, and patterns directly in source control alongside codebase changes.
patterns.context: Continuous architecture requires versioned, human-readable, and machine-inspectable knowledge bases.
forces: Architectural knowledge must live with code in Git rather than in isolated databases.
Knowledge structures require standard templates to guide documentation consistency.
patterns.solution: Structure the repository with distinct directories (cas-knowledge/templates, cas-knowledge/global, cas-knowledge/projects) and enforce standard markdown templates.
implementation_signals: Standardized markdown template names (e.g. architecture_decision_record_template.md, rule_template.md)
Segregation between templates/, global/, and projects/ directories
Bootstrap utilities to initialize workspaces from templates

evidence.note: Standardized ADR layout for repository knowledge capture
Populates workspace file structures according to convention hierarchy

benefits: Zero operational database overhead; all governance data is Git-trackable and branchable.
Seamless integration with static site documentation tools (MkDocs).
costs: File system operations lack ACID guarantees without custom locking or Git commits.
Requires strict linting/schema checking to prevent markdown template drift.
failure_modes: Malformed files or manual human edits disrupting automated parsing.

patterns.reuse_notes: Foundation for GitOps-style architecture documentation repositories.

anti_patterns.name: Stringly-Typed Path Traversal
symptoms: Direct manipulation of raw path strings rather than structured Pathlib objects in bootstrap functions
Manual string concatenation for building knowledge repository directory paths
impact: Cross-platform path delimiter issues (Windows vs POSIX)
Potential directory traversal bugs if inputs are not validated
suggested_remediation: Enforce pathlib.Path throughout bootstrap and runner modules.
Encapsulate repository layout behind a dedicated WorkspacePathResolver class.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Schema Exception Bubbling
symptoms: Pydantic ValidationErrors bubble directly up to CLI main
Generic stack traces displayed to end users when knowledge artifacts fail schema validation
impact: Difficulty identifying which specific template or markdown document caused the validation failure
suggested_remediation: Catch ValidationError at the ingestion layer and map to domain ComplianceFinding or GovernanceException with filename and line coordinates.

cross_cutting_concerns.description: SDK and API dependencies present for tracing system operations and compliance run passes across service boundaries.
Integrated documentation pipeline linking governance artifacts, ADRs, and diagrams via MkDocs and drawio plugins.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent filesystem writes coordinated across parallel CI/CD runners?
open_questions.context: The repository uses local file persistence (cas-knowledge/runtime/) which may conflict if multiple workflow jobs run simultaneously.

open_questions.question: Are transition registry configurations statically defined or dynamically loaded from YAML manifests at runtime?
open_questions.context: TransitionRegistry exists in governance_action_engine.py, but registration points could be expanded via plugin hooks.
